title: Fabric Architecture Implementation — Readiness and Scale Gates
purpose: Prevents a Fabric architecture from scaling before identity, environment, end-to-end value, operations, and recovery are proven.
accessibleSummary: A three-gate decision path. First confirm identity, ownership, and environments are ready. If they are not, stop and establish the delivery foundation. If they are, prove one end-to-end slice. Only a slice with quality, monitoring, rollback, replay, and support evidence advances to repeatable scale.
longDescription: The decision path is intentionally conservative. The first gate checks ownership, identity, environment configuration, and source/output contracts. The second gate asks whether a real vertical slice demonstrates business value through ingestion, transformation, serving, and consumption. The final outcome allows scaling only after operational acceptance. These are architecture patterns rather than Fabric product guarantees, so they are labelled as patterns and carry no fabricated evidence.

nodes.label: Are foundations ready?
nodes.summary: Confirm ownership, identity, environments, contracts, and recovery expectations before building the vertical slice.
nodes.detail: Readiness means named ownership, deployable environments, least-privilege identities, externalized configuration, a versioned source contract, and an explicit recovery expectation. A missing foundation is a stop condition, not a reason to hide manual work inside the first pipeline.
nodes.whyItMatters: The first production failure otherwise becomes the moment the team discovers it cannot reproduce configuration, rotate credentials, or identify who owns the data contract.

processing: Verify deployable configuration and least privilege
outputs: Go decision for one thin slice
Or a visible foundation backlog with owners
drill.example: A sales implementation pauses because its production service identity and rollback location are not approved, even though the development notebook already works.
failureModes: Treating a developer credential as production identity

nodes.label: Can one slice prove value?
nodes.summary: Deliver one source-to-consumer path that proves the real workload, data, security, deployment, and operating hand-offs.
nodes.detail: The slice must be vertical rather than a disconnected platform component: it ingests or references real data, applies one meaningful transformation, publishes a consumption contract, and demonstrates deployment and failure handling.
nodes.whyItMatters: A reusable framework built before one real slice tends to optimize imagined commonality and postpone the hardest integration and ownership decisions.

processing: Exercise one controlled failure and recovery
outputs: Evidence for or against reusable abstractions
drill.example: The slice copies one CRM entity, conforms it, builds one warehouse fact, and serves one certified report through automated dev-to-test deployment.
failureModes: Calling isolated infrastructure a vertical slice
Demo data hides real security behavior
Success path works but retry duplicates output

nodes.label: Scale after operational acceptance
nodes.summary: Repeat the pattern only after monitoring, quality, replay, rollback, capacity, and support ownership are proven.
nodes.detail: Operational acceptance is the final gate. The slice must expose completion, freshness, quality, and capacity signals; preserve a safe serving state during partial failure; and provide a tested procedure for replay, rollback, and escalation.
nodes.whyItMatters: Scaling an unaccepted pattern multiplies hidden manual steps and ambiguous failure ownership across every new source and domain.

inputs: Run, quality, freshness, and capacity evidence
processing: Review service objectives and failure evidence
Confirm replay and rollback are deterministic
drill.example: The sales slice scales to finance only after an operator successfully diagnoses a failed load, replays it without duplicates, and verifies consumers never saw partial output.
failureModes: Scaling after a demo instead of an operated run
Recovery procedure exists but has never been exercised

edges.label: yes — build one bounded vertical slice
no — scaling is blocked until foundations exist
value and recovery proven — seek operational acceptance
acceptance gap — harden and retest the slice

walkthrough.title: 1. Establish foundations
walkthrough.explanation: Do not build past missing ownership, identity, environment, contract, or recovery prerequisites.

walkthrough.title: 2. Prove one end-to-end slice
walkthrough.explanation: Use real data and a real consumer to expose the actual architecture hand-offs.

walkthrough.title: 3. Scale only after acceptance
walkthrough.explanation: Operational evidence determines whether the pattern is ready to repeat or must return for hardening.
